title: Place voters, then remove a failure domain
description: Choose an ensemble, spread its voting members, and inject a failure. The lab counts surviving voters against the majority required for writes.

ensembles.label: 3 voting members
ensembles.detail: Tolerates one voter failure. Appropriate for many bounded coordination workloads.

ensembles.label: 5 voting members
ensembles.detail: Tolerates two voter failures, with more replication and write acknowledgement work.

ensembles.label: 7 voting members
ensembles.detail: Tolerates three voter failures, but usually adds more cost and write latency than coordination needs justify.

placements.label: One rack
placements.detail: Every voter shares one power, network, and maintenance boundary.

placements.label: Two zones
placements.detail: The larger side holds a majority, so losing that side stops quorum.

placements.label: Three zones
placements.detail: Balanced placement can lose any one zone while retaining a majority.

failures.label: No failure
failures.detail: All voting members can exchange heartbeats and acknowledgements.

failures.label: Lose one voter
failures.detail: A process, host, or isolated member becomes unavailable.

failures.label: Lose the largest domain
failures.detail: Remove the rack or zone that contains the most voting members.

failures.label: Maintenance plus failure
failures.detail: One voter is intentionally offline and another fails unexpectedly.
